oracle_provenance.sql: Computed directly against the ai_v1_bq_* semantic views in MySQL `mcp_prod_wire_eval` - the same views the SQL route reads, queried without the planner, the LLM, or the RAG service. Every value carries the exact statement that produced it. All values independently re-derived during cold review.
oracle_provenance.documents: Read verbatim from data/corpus/company/<tier>/*.md in this repo.
oracle_provenance.authorization: Derived from app/rag/access_tiers.py (document tiers) and the BQ bundle's required_permissions (structured capabilities), cross-checked against each seeded user's live Spatie permissions and against billing's DocumentTierMapper, which is a port of get_access_tiers.
oracle_provenance.measure_semantics: An oracle must match what the PRODUCT computes, not merely what the question sounds like. ac-05 originally counted every APPROVED inventory row (2494); the bundle has no such measure, only stock_receipts_approved (type='Receive' AND status='APPROVED', = 100). The suite would have failed a correct answer. When adding a case, find the measure first and write the oracle from its filter_sql.
oracle_provenance.warning: Oracles are data-dependent. Re-derive them with tools/derive_oracles.sql after any ingest, restore, or migration of mcp_prod_wire_eval.

Two databases are live on this host and they are not the same one. The billing app (artisan serve, login, record views) reads mcp_local; the RAG container reads mcp_prod_wire_eval (MCP_BILLING_DATABASE_URL and MCP_RECORD_DATABASE_URL). That does not affect answers: no module under app/ reads a users table, and caller identity plus permissions arrive in the signed JWT record_access claim (app/auth/jwt.py:89-99, 155-170; ScopeValues in app/auth/record_access.py:48-56 accepts department_id only, extra=forbid). cases.title: Department scope applies - printing sees only its own jobs
cases.question: How many jobs do we have?

oracle.statement: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ai_v1_bq_job_fact WHERE entity_id=1 AND department_id=2

checks.why: The unscoped total. Its appearance means the forced department predicate was dropped.

cases.escalate_if: Answer is 6113 - authorization leakage across departments.

cases.title: Follow-up chips are grounded in the manifest and bounded
cases.question: (no new question - inspect the chips rendered on rb-01's answer)

oracle.derivation: _detect_resource matches 'jobs' in the question and resolves resource_type='job'. record_analytics_mode is disabled, so the count and group_count templates are withheld; the manifest's job resource has 'list', leaving exactly the one template (app/services/follow_up_suggestions.py:140-157).

checks.tolerance: Pluralisation may differ; the resource named must be jobs.

checks.why: Every chip must name a resource this caller's snapshot actually grants. A chip is a promise; offering an unreachable resource produces a guaranteed dead end.

cases.known_limitation: This case does NOT prove the chip permission gate. Chip TEXT is question-driven: _manifest_grounded_suggestions(resource_type, manifest) takes no principal, and _reachable_resources only decides which resources _detect_resource may match. Two callers who both hold `job` therefore get identical chips, and a caller who lacks it gets a denial - a path on which the UI suppresses chips anyway (renderAssistantMessageHtml gates on !msg.error). So no browser-observable comparison distinguishes the gate. The gate is covered by tests/services/test_follow_up_suggestions.py; do not report browser coverage of it.

cases.title: Department scope applies - store sees a different count for the same question
cases.question: How many jobs do we have?

oracle.statement: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ai_v1_bq_job_fact WHERE entity_id=1 AND department_id=1

checks.why: Identical question, two departments. Equal answers mean the scope value is ignored or hardcoded.

cases.title: No department on the caller - no department predicate
cases.question: How many jobs do we have?

oracle.statement: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ai_v1_bq_job_fact WHERE entity_id=1

checks.why: Three callers, one question, three correct answers. This triplet is the department-scope gate. Any two matching means scope is not derived from the caller.

cases.escalate_if: Answer is 7 or 6 - the scope predicate is being applied to a caller who has no department, which would silently hide 6,100+ rows from an administrator.

cases.title: Concurrency - the scope triplet fired simultaneously must not bleed
cases.question: How many jobs do we have?
cases.run_with: scripts/smoke/ask_concurrency_probe.py --rounds 5   (NOT the browser executor - an agent cannot fire three clicks simultaneously, and simultaneity is the entire test)

oracle.statement: Same statements as rb-01 / rb-02 / rb-03.

checks.why: One identical question with three DIFFERENT correct answers. Any other question gives every caller the same number, so a bleed would be invisible; here a bleed names itself.
Printing returning 6113 is not a wrong answer, it is ADMIN's answer. Distinguish the two - one is a scope bug, the other is a race.
Two callers returning the same leading number means one request's scope served another's answer.

cases.why_this_case_exists: The sequential suite never has two callers in flight at once, so it structurally cannot see a race. The RAG record path holds process-wide singletons - _RECORD_ENGINE and _ADAPTER_EXECUTOR (app/business_query/composition.py:66,84) - shared across concurrent requests. The other caches on this path (bundle_loader, retriever_factory, follow_up_suggestions) are keyed on deployment artifacts rather than on the caller, so they are not a bleed surface; the shared executor is.
cases.interpretation: Run ONLY after rb-01/rb-02/rb-03 pass sequentially. Passing apart and failing together implicates concurrency; failing in both is a scope bug and this case adds nothing. Races are probabilistic: a clean run means 'not observed in N rounds', never 'proven safe'. A dirty run is conclusive.
cases.escalate_if: Any caller returns another caller's expected value. This is cross-account authorization bleed - the most severe defect class the suite can surface, and it would be invisible to every other case.

cases.title: Capability denial - sales has no `view job`
cases.question: How many jobs are in progress right now?

checks.why: `view job` is absent from this caller's permissions; its snapshot has no `job` resource.

Pair this with the try-again check below. Alone, dom_absent(.try-again) passes vacuously whenever the denial arrives as ordinary prose rather than an error, so it would keep passing even if the retry-suppression logic were deleted.
A permanent capability gap is not a transient failure. Offering 'Try again' teaches the user to retry something that can never succeed.

checks.note: Does the decline say what the user CAN do, without leaking internal jargon (SQL, policy mode, manifest)?

cases.escalate_if: Any job count is disclosed.

cases.question: What is our total outstanding invoice balance?

cases.title: Simple count - customers
cases.question: How many customers do we have?

oracle.statement: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ai_v1_bq_customer_fact WHERE entity_id=1

checks.accept: No measure in the bundle is owned by `customer`, so 812 is reachable only through an entity_rows plan's total_row_count, which the presenter renders as 'Showing N of 812' (N is the planner-chosen page size, 1..50, default 20 - presenter.py:349-353; 1.7.3 corrected the stale 'Showing 50' example, review Minor 1). That IS a correct answer - do not require a scalar.

cases.title: New conversation isolates context
cases.question: How many are unpaid?

oracle.why: Asked immediately after clicking New conversation, this dangling question has no antecedent. The system must not silently inherit 'customers' from the cleared thread.

cases.procedure: Run the previous case to completion in this thread. Click [data-mcp-ask-new]. Confirm the thread is visually empty and screenshot that state. Then send the question above.

checks.why: The prior turn must be gone from the panel after New conversation.
The answer must not resolve 'unpaid' against the customer question from the cleared thread.

cases.title: Multi-clause count - total and unpaid invoices in one question
cases.question: How many invoices do we have in total, and how many of them are still unpaid?

oracle.statement: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ai_v1_bq_bill_fact WHERE entity_id=1 AND type='Invoice'   /   same + AND outstanding > 0
oracle.measure_check: invoices_count = COUNT(id) on a resource carrying record_predicates {type: Invoice}; invoices_unpaid has filter_sql 'outstanding > 0'. Both confirmed against the bundle - the predicates match the product.

checks.why: A dropped clause is the defect this case exists to catch.

cases.note: A plan carries exactly one measure in scalar shape, so answering both clauses in one turn needs a grouped plan. If only one clause is delivered, grade it a completeness defect AND record the plan shape - the fix would be in the planner, not the prompt.

cases.title: Top-N grouping - rendered as structure, in the right order
cases.question: Who are our top 5 customers by total invoiced amount?

oracle.statement: SELECT customer_name, ROUND(SUM(items_total),2) FROM ai_v1_bq_bill_fact WHERE entity_id=1 AND type='Invoice' GROUP BY customer_name ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5
oracle.currency: TZS - all 3520 invoices. Grouping by customer_name and by customer_id give the identical top 8, no ties.

checks.tolerance: Names must match and the ORDER must match. Amounts may be rounded or abbreviated but must not contradict. A currency column is EXPECTED, not a contradiction: bill_amount declares a currency_dimension and the preconditions force the plan to carry invoice.currency_code.

checks.why: Five ranked rows presented as one prose blob is a rendering defect, not a formatting preference.

cases.question: (click the first chip rendered on the previous answer)
